project.title: Community Profiling for Dead Game Classification Using Girvan-Newman Algorithm
project.primary_objective: Identify community profiles that characterize dead games in the Steam gaming platform ecosystem

research_problem.description: Understanding which game features and community characteristics are most associated with 'dead' games (games with very low or no active player base)
research_problem.motivation: Game developers and publishers need to understand what factors lead to game failure to make better development and marketing decisions
key_questions: What feature profiles characterize communities with high concentrations of dead games?
Can we predict if a new game will become dead based on its similarity to existing dead game communities?
Which game attributes (genre, price, developer, etc.) are most predictive of game failure?
How well do dead game communities generalize to unseen games?

methodology.approach: Train-Test Community Profiling with Girvan-Newman Algorithm
methodology.description: We use a novel approach that separates training and testing data to avoid overfitting in community detection and create generalizable profiles of dead games

1_data_preparation.description: Prepare game dataset with features and dead/alive labels

2_train_test_split.description: Randomly split games into training (80%) and testing (20%) sets to enable unbiased evaluation
2_train_test_split.rationale: Prevents overfitting by ensuring communities are discovered on training data only, then tested on truly unseen games

parameters.test_ratio: 0.2 (20% of games held out for testing)
parameters.stratification: None (simple random split to maintain natural game distribution)

3_similarity_graph_construction.description: Build cosine similarity graph between games based on feature vectors
3_similarity_graph_construction.process: Calculate pairwise cosine similarity between game feature vectors, keep edges above threshold

parameters.top_k_edges: 100 per node (limit edges for computational efficiency)
parameters.edge_filtering: Only include edges between training games for community detection

4_community_detection.description: Detect communities in the training game similarity graph by iteratively removing edges with highest betweenness centrality
4_community_detection.why_girvan_newman: Reveals hierarchical community structure and can identify communities of different sizes, important for finding diverse dead game profiles
4_community_detection.training_only: CRITICAL: Algorithm runs only on training games to avoid data leakage

parameters.selection_criteria: Choose community level with highest modularity score

5_community_profiling.description: Create characteristic profiles for each community by averaging feature vectors of member games
5_community_profiling.process: For each community, compute mean feature vector across all training games in that community
5_community_profiling.dead_game_focus: Identify communities with high concentrations of dead games as 'dead game profiles'

6_test_game_assignment.description: Assign test games to communities using cosine similarity with community profiles
6_test_game_assignment.process: For each test game, calculate cosine similarity with each community profile, assign to most similar community
6_test_game_assignment.similarity_metric: Cosine similarity between test game feature vector and community average feature vector
6_test_game_assignment.assignment_rule: Assign to community with highest similarity score

7_evaluation_and_validation.description: Evaluate how well the community profiling system performs on unseen test games

metrics.similarity_scores: Distribution of cosine similarity scores between test games and assigned communities (higher = better match)
metrics.community_coverage: Percentage of communities that receive at least one test game assignment
metrics.assignment_balance: Whether test games are distributed proportionally across communities
metrics.dead_game_prediction: How well communities with high dead game ratios attract test games that are also dead

methodology.key_innovation: Train-test separation ensures that community profiles are discovered without knowledge of test games, enabling unbiased evaluation of how well dead game profiles generalize to unseen games

target_variable.name: is_dead / label_dead_binary
target_variable.description: Binary label indicating whether a game is 'dead' (very low/no active players) or 'alive' (active player base)
target_variable.determination_method: Based on player count data from SteamCharts - games with consistently very low player counts are labeled as dead

data_description.feature_engineering: Features are encoded as sparse matrices using one-hot encoding, hash encoding, and normalization

primary_findings: Community profiles that characterize dead games (e.g., specific genre combinations, price points, developer patterns)
Quantitative measure of how well dead game communities generalize to unseen games
Identification of game features most predictive of belonging to dead game communities

success_criteria.high_similarity_scores: Mean cosine similarity > 0.7 indicates good community-game matching
success_criteria.good_coverage: Community coverage > 80% shows profiles are broadly applicable
success_criteria.predictive_power: Dead game communities successfully attract test games that are also dead

applications: Recommendation systems based on community profiles
Early warning systems for potentially failing games

technical_implementation.computational_requirements: Moderate - can handle ~16K games on standard desktop hardware
technical_implementation.scalability: Scales to larger datasets with sparse matrix operations and efficient graph algorithms
technical_implementation.reproducibility: Fixed random seeds and detailed parameter logging ensure reproducible results

validation_approach.train_test_separation: Strict separation prevents data leakage and overfitting
validation_approach.cross_validation_potential: Can be extended with multiple random splits for robustness testing
validation_approach.baseline_comparisons: Compare against random assignment and simple feature-based clustering
validation_approach.statistical_testing: Evaluate significance of community-dead game associations

assumptions: Games with similar features should belong to similar communities
Dead/alive labels are accurate and stable over time
Feature representation captures important game characteristics
Cosine similarity is appropriate metric for game similarity
limitations: Static analysis - doesn't account for temporal changes in game popularity
Feature selection may miss important predictive attributes
Community detection is computationally expensive for very large graphs
Binary dead/alive classification may oversimplify game health spectrum

for_llms.key_concept: This is a machine learning methodology that uses unsupervised community detection (Girvan-Newman) combined with supervised evaluation to find patterns in game failure
for_llms.novelty: The train-test split applied to community detection prevents overfitting and enables rigorous evaluation of community profiles
for_llms.domain_relevance: Addresses real business problem in gaming industry about predicting and understanding game failure
for_llms.methodological_strength: Combines graph theory, community detection, and similarity metrics in a principled evaluation framework
